tr.td: Establishing primary care for type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure above goal: A1c, kidney function, urine albumin, lipids, the yearly liver check with FIB-4, eyes, feet and brain health in a former professional boxer
Two-week review of home blood pressure readings, with liver elastography, a liver ultrasound and the hepatology consultation
Eight-week review: blood pressure, lipids, kidney function, semaglutide, the endoscopy result and vaccines
Three-month review: A1c, blood pressure, weight, semaglutide dose and the eye examination
Seven-month review: six-month liver cancer surveillance ultrasound and AFP, A1c, kidney function, urine albumin and vaccines

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diabetes: continue metformin, an A1c every three months until at goal and then every six months, diabetes self-management education, a vitamin B12 check on long-term metformin, and no medicine that causes low blood sugar
Hepatology consultation for a high FIB-4 with mildly low platelets, with transient elastography and a liver ultrasound the same day
Liver assessment: FIB-4 from the yearly liver tests, then transient elastography if FIB-4 is 1.3 or higher; hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests, iron studies, and an alcohol history

Compensated cirrhosis: liver ultrasound with AFP every six months for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, upper endoscopy to screen for varices, hepatitis A and B and pneumococcal vaccines, no alcohol, no NSAIDs, acetaminophen no more than 2 g a day, and teaching on the warning signs of decompensation

Semaglutide once weekly, increased every four to eight weeks as tolerated, for its cardiovascular and kidney benefit, weight and steatotic liver disease; prior authorization and the manufacturer's assistance program handled by the clinic
Blood pressure: a validated home monitor with a large cuff, readings twice a day for a week, a goal below 130/80 mmHg, and less salt
Amlodipine added to lisinopril and increased to reach the goal, with ankle-swelling checks
Cardiovascular risk: atorvastatin 40 mg with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks; a baseline ECG; aspirin for primary prevention not used because of bleeding risk
Kidneys: eGFR by the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio at least yearly, and potassium and creatinine on lisinopril
Eyes and feet: a dilated eye examination at the eye clinic, a comprehensive foot examination yearly, daily foot checks and callus care

Brain health: a documented cognitive screen at the preventive visit, blood pressure and glucose control, sleep, hearing and mood checks, and an honest conversation that chronic traumatic encephalopathy cannot be diagnosed during life
Cost and access: low-cost generics, 90-day supplies, and help with coverage for any brand-name medicine
A1c below 7% within six to nine months, without low blood sugar
8.4% to 6.8% at seven months; no low blood sugar
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg in the clinic and at home
Weight loss of 7 to 10% for liver health within a year
Liver cancer surveillance by ultrasound with AFP every six months, on time
Baseline and six-month ultrasounds with AFP on schedule; no focal lesion; AFP 4.2 and 4.0 ng/mL
No alcohol, to protect the liver
No alcohol since the two-week visit
